title: GSK Eyes Nearly Doubling Cancer Drug Pipeline in 2027, Targets 19-20 Late-Stage Studies

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: GSK expects to nearly double the number of cancer medicines it is testing in clinical trials next year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing an interview with a scientist at the British drugmaker.

Hesham Abdullah, GSK's head of oncology research and development, told the WSJ that the company's clinical-stage portfolio of about 15 assets is likely to come close to doubling in 2027

According to the report, Abdullah said GSK could have 19 to 20 late-stage oncology studies underway next year, with drug candidates being moved straight from early-stage to late-stage studies to speed development.

GSK did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

The drugmaker's oncology push is part of CEO Luke Miels' effort to reassure investors that GSK can navigate a looming patent cliff for its blockbuster HIV drugs

In July, GSK said it expected to have more than 20 late-stage studies by the end of 2026, with three of the seven drugs identified for faster development being cancer medicines

The company is rebuilding its oncology portfolio after exiting the space more than a decade ago, with cancer drugs such as ris-rez and mo-rez at the centre of its strategy

Its oncology segment contributed £1.08 billion ($1.44 billion) in the first half of 2026.

Source : Reuters
